 Judgment

The appellant/accused was convicted by the Trial Court in S.C.No.30 of 2020 by the judgment dated 23.02.2022 for the offence under Section 376 r/w 375 r/w 90 IPC and sentenced to undergo ten years Rigorous Imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-, in default, further period of three months of Simple Imprisonment.

Though charge was framed under Section 417 IPC, the trial Court held that since it is the small part of misconception of fact which is covered under Section 90 IPC,
no separate sentence is imposed for the above said offence.
2.The case of the prosecution is that PW1/defacto complainant is a victim who had a love affair with the appellant from 2015 onwards.
The appellant and defacto complainant's mother worked in the same company, and he used to visit her house frequently.

On 25.12.2018 at 2.00 p.m the appellant came to PW1's house, induced her with a promise that he would marry her and had forceful sexual relationship with her though she refused, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
23/10/2025 01:24:38 pm ) hence, committed rape on her against her will and without her consent.
Subsequently, on several occasions, both had physical relationship.

The defacto complainant's father/PW2 on coming to know about the relationship, enquired her daughter/PW1, who informed appellant committed forceful physical relationship on her on the promise of marriage.
On 01.04.2019, the victim called the appellant requesting him to marry her, but the appellant refused and informed he is to marry another girl.

Thereafter, PW1 lodged a complaint to the respondent Police on 05.04.2019, and the case in Crime No.7 of 2019 for the offence under Sections 376 and 417 IPC registered by the Inspector of Police/PW15.
After registration of FIR, PW16 conducted investigation, visited the scene of occurrence, prepared rough sketch, observation mahazar in presence of witnesses PW3 and PW4.

The victim's father, neighbours and relatives all examined,
and their statements confirmed victim and appellant loved each other and seen together in several places including isolated places.
The victim referred for medical test.
PW14, Doctor, examined the victim, issued medical certificate/Ex.P.6 giving opinion https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

Subsequently, the victim appeared before the Magistrate, on 03.07.2019 and her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C./Ex.P2 recorded.
The appellant after his arrest produced before PW10/Doctor, who gave Potency Certificate/Ex.P5.

On conclusion of investigation, charge sheet filed against the appellant under Sections 376 and 417 IPC and the case was tried by the learned Sessions Judge, Magalir Neethi Mandram (Fast Track Court), Villupuram in S.C.No.30 of 2020.
3.During trial, on the side of the prosecution PW1 to PW16 examined, Exs.P1 to P11 marked.
On the side of the defence, no witnesses examined and no exhibits marked.
On conclusion of trial, the trial Court convicted the appellant as above.
Aggrieved over the same, the appellat filed the present Criminal Appeal.

sentences.text:
Both of them attained majority, developed interest had close and intimate relationship,
the marriage proposal between them contemplated and their physical relationship was mutual and consensual.

The Doctor/PW14 who examined the victim in her report (Ex.P6) recorded the relationship between the appellant and the victim for past four years, the victim confirms physical relationship and no injuries found on her body confirming it was not a forceful act.
On examination of external genetalia, no injuries were present, confirming relationship is consensual with concurrence.
Later, the victim's mother passed away on 14.03.2019.
Till such time, their intimate relationship was not questioned.
The marriage between the appellant and victim could not be performed due to victim's father creating obstacles.
Subsequently, marriage between the appellant with another lady arranged.
The victim in impulsive reacted and lodged a complaint alleging it is the a p p e l l a n t w h o r e f u s e d t o m a r r y h e r .

the appellant cannot be blamed.

5.The learned counsel further submitted that the neighbours and family members PW5, PW6, PW7,
PW8 and PW9 all confirm love relationship between the appellant and the victim.

Since the victim had a broken heart for not getting married to the appellant, she lodged a complaint which is quite natural and blamming the appellant as though he made false promise and committed rape is not proper.

The documents and evidence confirms the love relationship between the appellant and victim, no injuries both internal and external found in the parts or anywhere on the victim's body leading to inference of consensual relationship.
In this case, both are majors having consensual relationship knowing its consequences.

6.Today, the learned counsel for appellant produced a joint compromise memo filed by the appellant and the defacto complainant confirming that the appellant and the defacto complainant have now buried hatchet resolved the dispute between them.

Both of them are now married https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 23/10/2025 01:24:38 pm ) but separately and living with their respective families.
7.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent Police opposed the appellant's contention and submitted that the victim lodged a complaint, and the complaint Ex.P.1 was registered on 05.04.2019.

In the complaint, she has specifically stated that the appellant and the victim's mother were working in the same company, the appellant used to visit the victim's house frequently and shown interest on her and both developed a love relationship for four years.
Taking advantage of the relationship, whenever the victim was alone in her house, the appellant used to come to her house and they were talking in closeness.
The appellant, on the false promise of marriage had a forcible physical relationship with the victim.
Later, the victim's mother passed away on 14.03.2019.
Thereafter, the appellant stopped visiting the victim's house, and he planned to marry another lady.

sentences.text: The victim was sent for medical examination.
PW14/Doctor examined her and issued medical report Exs.P6 & P7.
The accused was arrested, and he was produced for medical examination.
PW10/Doctor examined the appellant and issued potency report/Ex.P5.
The victim appeared before the Magistrate and gave statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C confirming the complaint.
On collection of evidence and materials, charge sheet filed in this case.
During the trial, all the witnesses examined confirmed the prosecution case.
The trial Court considering the evidence and materials produced, convicted the appellant for offence under Section 376 r/w 375 r/w 90 IPC.

8.This Court considered the rival submissions and perused the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 23/10/2025 01:24:38 pm )
9.It is not in dispute that the appellant and the victim are relatives and they had known each other and loved each other for nearly four years and had physical relationship on several occasions.
Both the appellant and victim are educated persons, and they knowingly had a close relationship unmindful of consequences.
Only when the victim came to know that the appellant was planning to marry another girl, she lodged the complaint to the respondent Police.
All the other witnesses confirmed the love relationship between the victim and appellant seeing them together in several places in closeness.
10.It is seen that in this case the appellant confined in prison from 06.04.2019 to 23.05.2019.
Now the appellant and victim are married to different partners and are living happily with their respective families.

In view of the above, confirming the conviction of the appellant for offence under Section 376 Cr.P.C would not be proper, hence, this Court is inclined to set aside the conviction and sentence for offence under Section 375 r/w 90 r/w 376 IPC.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

11.In this case, the appellant was charged and convicted for offence under Section 417 IPC but no separate sentence passed, hence, the conviction for offence under Section 417 IPC against the appellant is sustained.
In view of the compromise between the appellant and victim and the offence under Section 417 IPC is compoundable, this Court compounds the offence under Section 417 IPC for the following reasons.

12.Today, the appellant and the victim appeared before this Court and filed joint compromise memo signed by both the parties, which reads as follows:
1.The above appeal is filed challenging the order of conviction by the Court of Sessions Judge Magalir Neethi Mandram (Fast Track Mahila Court), Villupuram in S.C. No.30 of 2020 dated 23.02.2022, convicting the appellant under Section 376 IPC, and imposed a sentence of 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.25,000/- with default sentence of 3 months simple imprisonment and compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: The appellant used to come the defacto complainants house regularly till the death of the defacto complainant's mother on 14.3.2019.
Subsequently had stopped coming.
The appellant's marriage was fixed with another girl.
Since the appellant had failed to marry, the defacto complainant, the complaint was lodged on 5.4.2019 for the offence under Section 417 and 376 IPC.
The defacto complainant states that now she has married another person and is settled with her family.
The Appellant also married the girl with whom, the marriage was finalized and living with his family.
Both the Appellant and the defacto complainant had compromised the issue and the defacto complainant has no objection in acquitting the appellant.

For the foregoing reasons it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased allow the appeal and acquit https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 23/10/2025 01:24:38 pm ) the appellant recording the compromise memo signed by both the parties.

13.This Court interacted with both the appellant and victim/PW1 and they confirmed the relationship and informed that both got married but with different partners and are living happily with their respective family.
The victim agreed to compound the offence considering their past relationship and future well-being of both of them and their respective families.

14.Accordingly, this Criminal Appeal is allowed in terms of Joint Compromise Memo dated 08.10.2025 and the judgment dated 23.02.2022 in S.C.No.30 of 2020 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Magalir Neethi Mandram (Fast Track Mahila Court) Villupuram is set aside.
